planner: Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM) system and sensors denied (MN-04) on 2026-09-22

strategy: Lead with the policy-misapplication argument, which is likely dispositive. The denial relies on an intensive-insulin requirement (3+ daily injections or a pump) that, per the policy document provided, was removed from MP-DME-031 in the 01/01/2026 revision. The service was requested 2026-09-18 and denied 2026-09-22, so the current version governs. The member independently meets two current criteria: (1) I.B.1, any insulin regimen, because she uses nightly insulin glargine; and (2) I.B.2, documented problematic hypoglycemia, because of two level 2 nocturnal episodes, recurrence despite dose reduction, living alone, and neuropathy limiting fingerstick testing. Ask that the denial be overturned on either criterion. Support this with clinical evidence: ADA Standards of Care recommendations for CGM in insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, including basal-only regimens and people with hypoglycemia; the Medicare CGM LCD, which covers any insulin use or problematic hypoglycemia; and RCT evidence (e.g., the MOBILE trial) for CGM in basal-insulin type 2 diabetes. Request a same-or-similar-specialty (endocrinology) peer reviewer and the reviewer's criteria and credentials. Request a peer-to-peer discussion if available. Build the packet around: an endocrinologist letter of medical necessity citing I.B.1 and I.B.2 by number; meter downloads or logs documenting both episodes; the 2026-09-10 visit note and labs; documentation of diabetes educator training; the device model and FDA labeling; a copy of the current MP-DME-031 showing the 01/01/2026 revision; and an Appointment of Representative form if the clinic files. Note any other issues raised in the denial and address them preemptively, such as training or a visit within 6 months, which are already documented.

discrepancy: Outdated criterion applied: the denial requires '3 or more daily injections of insulin or use of an insulin pump.' The 01/01/2026 revision history of MP-DME-031 states this requirement was 'REMOVED.' It does not appear in the version in effect on the 09/18/2026 request date.

discrepancy: Self-contradicting finding: the denial's sole factual basis is that the member uses 'a once-daily long-acting insulin only.' Current Criterion I.B.1 expressly covers 'any insulin regimen, including a single daily dose of basal/long-acting insulin.' The plan's own finding therefore establishes that I.B is met.

discrepancy: Alternative pathway ignored: the denial never addresses I.B.2 (problematic hypoglycemia). The notes document two level 2 events (<54 mg/dL), the second despite an insulin dose reduction. It is unknown whether this history was in the records submitted on 09/18/2026; the prior authorization packet should be obtained to confirm.
discrepancy: No other criteria disputed: the denial does not claim that criteria A, C, D or E are unmet. The notes document each of them.
discrepancy: Version not identified: the denial cites MP-DME-031 without a version or effective date, and its paraphrase does not match the current policy text.

discrepancy: Appeal clock wording differs: the denial says the appeal must be received within 180 days of 'the date of this notice.' EOC 9.1 says 180 days 'of receiving' the determination. The safest course is to count from the 09/22/2026 notice date, which gives a deadline of 03/21/2027.

insurer would argue: Criterion I.E requires that the treating practitioner 'determined that criteria A through D are met.' The 09/10/2026 note contains no such determination, and the provider's support statement is a single sentence with no attestation. A reviewer looking for a new ground could say I.E is not documented.

insurer would argue: Criterion I.C: neither the note nor the letter names the CGM device. The reviewer could say the Plan cannot confirm the device is being prescribed within its FDA indications for an adult with type 2 diabetes on basal insulin, and that 'per FDA labeling' is a conclusory phrase.

insurer would argue: Expedited handling not warranted: both hypoglycemic events were self-treated, months apart, with no level 3 event. The attestation placeholder is blank, so the Plan could treat the request as standard. The letter's fallback to a 30-day standard appeal limits the harm.

insurer would argue: Criterion I.C: the progress note never names the CGM device, so FDA-labeled prescribing cannot be verified. The draft closes this gap with the Part A device-name field, the provider confirmation of FDA indications, and drafting note 1 forbidding sending with the field unfilled. It holds only if the clinic fills in the field before signing.

insurer would argue: Criterion I.E: the 09/10/2026 note has no explicit statement that criteria A–D were 'determined' met, so the determination may be post hoc. This is weak. The note documents each element (diagnosis, insulin, FDA-labeled prescribing, educator training) at the visit, and Part A states the determination was based on that evaluation. The policy does not require magic words.

insurer would argue: The records submitted with the 09/18/2026 request showed only once-daily insulin and nothing else. This does not help the plan. Under current I.B.1, once-daily basal insulin alone qualifies, and the full 09/10/2026 note is enclosed with the appeal.
